svg.title: End-to-End Distributed Web Crawler & Mercator Dual-Queue URL Frontier
svg.desc: Complete architectural pipeline of a distributed web crawler featuring a two-stage Mercator frontier with prioritized front queues and per-host back queues, min-heap politeness scheduler, asynchronous DNS cache, RFC 9309 robots.txt cache, streaming HTTP/2-3 downloader, 64-bit SimHash near-duplicate deduplication, URL normalization and spider trap defense, and an in-memory Bloom filter backed by sharded RocksDB LSM SSTables.
svg.text: End-to-End Distributed Web Crawler & Mercator Dual-Queue URL Frontier
Two-Stage Mercator Scheduling (Priority Front Queues + Politeness Back Queues) · Async DNS Cache · SimHash LSH Dedup · RocksDB/Bloom Loop
Alexa/Tranco top sites, sitemaps, RSS feeds
Search query logs & expired recrawl tasks
Poisson model estimates page change rate
Assigns priority tiers: F1 (top) to FK (low)
Biased random selector drains F1 > F2 > FK
Drained URLs stream to Back Queue Router
Back Queue Router & Host Mapping Table
hash(host) % M -> routes to Back Queue Bj
Host Table tracks active domain mappings dynamically
Invariant: Queue Bj contains URLs from 1 host only
Back Queues B1..BM (1 Queue per Host)
Strict FIFO order; isolates slow hosts from blocking fast ones
Pops head queue Bj only when now() >= next_allowed_fetch_time
Advances timer on dequeue; pushes Bj back into heap with new ts
Guarantees max 1 active request per host across entire fleet
Async I/O event loops (Rust tokio / Go epoll runtimes)
Pulls 1 URL from eligible Back Queue popped from heap
Passes target URL to non-blocking streaming downloader
Local Async DNS Cache & robots.txt Cache
Async DNS Cache: bypasses libc getaddrinfo() thread stalls
Caches A/AAAA IPs locally; round-robins multi-homed hosts
RFC 9309 robots.txt Cache: TTL 24h; parses Allow/Disallow
Treats 5xx as temporary disallow backoff; protects origins
Multiplexed streams over HTTP/2 & QUIC (0-RTT handshakes)
Conditional GET: ETag & If-Modified-Since (304 Not Modified)
Aggressive timeouts: 5s connect, 15s body; drop slow tarpits
Streams downloaded raw response body to Content Parser
Quantitative System Invariants & Mercator Scheduling Guarantees
Scale: 1B–10B pages/mo (400–4,000 pps avg, 800–12,000 QPS peak) · Wire: 10–100 MB/s gzip (40–400 MB/s raw) · Storage: 1.5 PB (1B/mo) / 3.65 PB (10B/mo net-new) / 5 yr
Politeness: Exactly 1 in-flight req per host; delay dt >= max(robots_delay, 10 * RTT) · DNS: Async in-memory resolver eliminates 200ms libc stalls
Deduplication: 64-bit SimHash (Hamming <= 3 via 4x16-bit blocks) cuts 35% duplicate crawl; Bloom (12 GB) + RocksDB LSM scales to 10B unique URLs
